'''INS ''Anvesh''''' ([[Hindi]]: अन्वेष; lit. ''Search''),<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.wisdomlib.org/definition/anvesa | title=Anvesa, Anvesha, Anveṣa: 9 definitions | date=3 August 2014 }}</ref> is a [[missile range instrumentation ship]] (also termed as a ''Floating Test Range'' (FTR)) built for the [[Indian Navy]]. The ship is a project of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO) and built by [[Cochin Shipyard Limited]] (CSL).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2021-09-07 |title=Sea trials for floating missile test range INS Anvesh begin this month |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/sea-trials-for-floating-missile-test-range-ins-anvesh-begin-this-month-101630984781024.html |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref>

The ship was conceived to serve as a sea-based platform for India's [[Indian Ballistic Missile Defence Programme|ballistic missile defence program]] and consists of 4 Ship Launch System (SLS) [[Vertical launching system|VLS]] for the same purpose. The Phase II of the BMD envisages intercepting and destroying enemy missile up to range of 5,000 kilometers by [[Kinetic energy weapon|kinetic force]] with the FTR allowing live testing of the [[interdictor]] missiles and not computer simulations.<ref name="thehindu" />

== Design ==
INS ''Anvesh'' was designed by [http://viksandvik.in/#home Vik-Sandvik Design India Pvt Ltd] ("VSDI").<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vik-Sandvik Design India - Ship Designs & Naval Architectural Services in India |url=http://viksandvik.in/ |access-date=2020-01-12 |website=viksandvik.in}}</ref> It has a length of 118.4 m, 20 m width and 7.1 m draft and having a steel weight of approximately 3,900 tons.<ref name="CSL">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=27 January 2017 |title=TDV Mega Block Erection |url=http://www.cochinshipyard.com/press/TDV_MEGA_BLOCK_ERECTION.pdf |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date= |website=[[Cochin Shipyard]]}}</ref>

The ship incorporates [[Electronics and Radar Development Establishment|LRDE]] Long-Range Multi Function Radar (LRMFR) which will be used by Indian naval ships in future as Fire control radars for Ballistic Missile Defence. The 6 metre Active [[Antenna array|Antenna Array]] Unit (AAAU) for the radar was built by [https://astramwp.com/ Astra Microwave Products Ltd.] the first of which would be delivered in latter half of 2023. The LRMFR is an S-band radar system which is intended to replace the [[EL/M-2248 MF-STAR]] radar used by the Indian Navy as the primary naval radar of the next generation of naval ships. The functions of LRMFR includes acting as [[Fire-control radar|Fire Control Radar]] (FCR) for [[surface-to-air missile]] systems onboard ships and to track [[Ballistic missile|ballistic missiles]].<ref>{{Cite twitter |number=1686410678649966592 |user=AdithyaKM_ |title=Astra Microwave's "6m S-band AAAU for strategic naval application of DRDO" is due for delivery in 2023-24 according... |date=2023-08-01 |access-date=2024-07-26}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2023-04-25 |title=India Conducts First Test of New Ship-Based BMD System |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2023/04/india-conducts-first-test-of-new-ship-based-bmd-system/ |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}}</ref>

The vessel equipped with [[Electro-optical sensor|electro-optical]] missile tracking, [[S band|S-band]] radar tracking, [[Telemetry device|telemetry devices]] apart from a launch pad, control and mission control center, for testing its Phase II of [[Indian Ballistic Missile Defence Programme|Ballistic Missile Defence]] (BMD) interceptor missiles. The Phase II of the BMD envisages intercepting and destroying enemy missile up to range of 5,000 kilometers by kinetic force with the FTR allowing live testing of the [[interdictor]] missiles and not computer simulations.<ref name=":0" />

The missile launch system consists of 4 Ship Launching Systems (SLS) in the [[List of ship directions|aft section]] which rests at 0° when not in used but the alignment is changed to 90° during test launches.<ref name="X-220621" /><ref name="X-111222" /> The SLS was developed by Electropneumatics & Hydraulics Pvt Ltd. The ship has other specialised systems like damping tanks, missile integration and checkout bay, data processing room and mission control center. It is also equipped with a 15 ton crane and A-frame for cargo handling in the aft section.<ref name=":1" />

It is also designed to test radars, sonars, telemetry equipment and propulsion. The configuration of the installed power generation is [[Integrated electric propulsion|Integrated Full Electric Propulsion]] (IFEP). The output is 14 MW which is produced by diesel generators powering steerable [[Contra-rotating#Marine propulsion|contra-rotating propulsion]] thrusters.<ref name=":1" />

== Construction ==

The construction of the then-DRDO Technology Demonstration Vessel was awarded to the [[Cochin Shipyard|Cochin Shipyard Limited]] (CSL) by the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation|DRDO]], India's premier agency for R&D in defence, in August 2015.<ref name=thehindu>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/cochin-shipyard-to-build-secret-vessel-for-drdo/article7902532.ece|title=Cochin Shipyard to build secret vessel for DRDO|last=Anandan|first=S.|date=2015-11-21|work=The Hindu|access-date=2017-07-17|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

The original contract for the construction of the vessel was with [[Bharati Shipyard]], but time overruns forced by the yard's poor finances led to termination of the contract. Subsequently, the Cochin Shipyard won the bid to execute this project.

Steel plate cutting of the vessel was started on 10 August 2016. [[S. Christopher|Dr. S Christopher]], chairman, DRDO and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D, launched the mega block assembly of hull blocks of the ship (Ship No. 20) on 27 January 2016 at CSL.<ref name=CSL/>

The ceremonial event of commencement of Mega Block Assembly of hull blocks of Ship No. 20, the Technology Demonstration Vessel, being built for the Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO), Government of India was held on 27 January 2017 at CSL.

It was reported that the ship will commence the sea trial in September 2021 and will be commissioned by the end of 2021.<ref name=":0" />

== Commissioning ==

The ship had been quietly commissioned by [[National Security Advisor (India)|National Security Advisor]] [[Ajit Doval]] on 11 March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2023-04-25 |title=India Conducts First Test of New Ship-Based BMD System |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2023/04/india-conducts-first-test-of-new-ship-based-bmd-system/ |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}}</ref> A photo of the commissioning ceremony has been made public for the first time in the Indian Navy Song 2022: 'Hum Taiyyar hain'.<ref>{{cite news|title=Indian Navy Song 2022: 'Hum Taiyyar hain'|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uf9zDKR7MW4&t=262s}}</ref>

== Service history ==
The first missile test onboard INS Anvesh was carried out on 21 April 2023 off the [[Odisha]] coast. The missile tested was an [[Indian Ballistic Missile Defence Programme#Advanced Air Defence (AAD)|Advanced Air Defence]] (AAD) or ''Ashwin'' Ballistic Missile Interceptor. The missile included India in the list of countries who have developed naval [[Ballistic Missile Defense|BMD]] systems.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-04-23 |title=India successfully carries out maiden flight-test of sea-based ballistic missile defence interceptor |url=https://theigmp.org/sea-based-ballistic-missile-defence-interceptor/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509063432/https://theigmp.org/sea-based-ballistic-missile-defence-interceptor/ |archive-date=9 May 2023 |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=IgMp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-22 |title=India showcases naval ballistic missile defence capability in maiden test |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/drdo-and-indian-navy-successfully-test-sea-based-endo-atmospheric-interceptor-missile-showcasing-india-s-naval-bmd-capabilities-missiledefence-drdo-indiannavy-bmd-ballisticmissiles-101682176497606.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422183108/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/drdo-and-indian-navy-successfully-test-sea-based-endo-atmospheric-interceptor-missile-showcasing-india-s-naval-bmd-capabilities-missiledefence-drdo-indiannavy-bmd-ballisticmissiles-101682176497606.html |archive-date=22 April 2023 |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>She participated at the [[International Fleet Review 2026]] held at [[Visakhapatnam|Visakapatanam]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=IFR & MILAN 2026 |url=https://www.ifrmilan26.com/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219124733/https://www.ifrmilan26.com/ |archive-date=2026-02-19 |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=IFR & MILAN 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
